form: entities = new entities in the strokes format (accept by copying, as gen/map/S4/second_pass/); edits = changes to existing entities (set: fields to replace; add_note: text to append to note; remove_members: for groups); retire = entities to drop with the reason (README rule 7); settled = merge questions answered with no change

entities.name: dark head at the mat shed's south-east corner post (or a lidded jar)
entities.what: A dark rounded head, seen from behind with no face showing, at the foot of the south-east corner post of the mat-roofed stall under the arch's south side: a person standing or squatting on the bank just east of the eating stall, everything below the head hidden behind the big hall's north gable roof. It could instead be a dark-lidded jar standing at the post's foot.
entities.vis: part: only the head shows; below v ~1285 hidden behind the north gable roof of S3.bld.bridge_foot_hall_19000
entities.note: SECOND PASS (east): t8 saw it and left it to t7 ('a dark shape by its post at (19318-19351, 1259-1288) (a seated figure's head, or a jar)'). t7 did not record it, so no entity covers it. Strokes: a dark dome 19318-19350, v 1259-1283, about 32 x 24 px, lighter below it to v ~1300. It sits right under the shed's east post (S3.bld.mat_shed_19160: post at u 19330-19340, v 1140-1300), and the hall's bargeboard passes below it at v ~1320. Its size fits the heads of the bank watchers nearby (25-30 px). It lies 100 px below the seated diners' heads (v 1138-1177), so it is not one of them: it stands in front of (south of) the stall. Foot est from a ~130 px figure height (S3.fig.under_parasol_bender_19385 ~123 px, S3.fig.bank_waver_19612 ~135 px). It lies inside the hall's roof area on the scan, as for the other hidden-foot figures here. facing_deg 90 because no face shows (back of the head). If the lead reads a jar, record a prop `S3.prop.jar_by_shed_post_19334` at base (19334, 1290, est) instead. Crops: p2e_c_shedpost_col.jpg, p2e_c_shedpost.jpg, p2e_c_stall_col.jpg.

As a man standing on the far deck (est foot v ~490-590) it would be about 185 px tall against 83-118 px for the crew. The proposed edit adds it to the boat's what as a third loop.

The arms of S3.fig.boatman_stern_bending_20365 (river_e's second reading). On a plain zoom-3.5 crop and a colour crop at zoom 2.5, the bending man's cap is at v 273-281 (u 20345-20365). His torso bends east, and his arms reach down to the box at the stern rail (20389-20411, v 313-344). At the recorded head (20394, 312) only his shoulder and sleeve show: there is no face, cap or separate hair mass. The poop holds three men: hauling (20205), seated (20285) and bending (20365).

Carried, not hung (t9's 'more likely reading'). The pole's east end rests on the shoulder of S3.fig.porter_with_pole_20450, at his head, and he is drawn in a walking stride. Its west end stops just short of the shop's corner post (20375-20383) with no joint, tie or bracket. The sack and the staff are his load, already in his what (note edit proposed).

lessons: Read faint things on a saturated colour crop at zoom 2-2.5 (sharp `modulate({saturation: 1.8})` plus `linear(1.25, -35)`, cubic upscale), not only on contrast-stretched greyscale. On S3's second pass the colour crop told planks from mat, a hull's iron cramps from the bridge's beams, and a parasol's far rim from a figure, where greyscale at zoom 3 and above showed only grain.

Before keeping a 'head' among ropes or under a bridge, look along the same structure for repeats. S3's 'head among the rigging' was the third of three hooks hanging under the arch's rib at regular spacing.

Check a doubtful figure's strokes against the ellipse of any parasol or canopy beside it. A canopy's far rim drawn against a dark mass reads as a light-robed body (S3's 'figure at the moored boat's bow').
Compare the units' left-to lists by u range, not only by name. S3's far-bank tables at 19353-19396 were left by t7 to t8 and by t8 to t7, so nobody recorded them.

Before merging a hat and a face into one man, or splitting them into two, measure the head's height against the faces around it. One tall hat over S3's round face would make a 58 px head among 20 px faces, so it is a second man behind.
